newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea shrugs off sharp fall in CBOT soy prices.
newsitem.headline: Korea shrugs off sharp fall in CBOT soy prices.

text.p: South Korean feed millers shrugged off the collapse in soybean and soymeal prices in the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), saying on Tuesday the fall was only temporary.
"The price fall looks like a brief consolidation," said Hong Soon-chang, a spokesman for the Korea Feed Association.
CBOT soybean futures dived after the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) said on Monday its 1996/97 soybean ending stocks were unchanged at 125 million bushels, dissapointing the market.
The CBOT soybean July contract fell 20-1/2 U.S. cents to end on Monday at US$8.68-1/2 a bushel. The July soymeal contract on the CBOT shed $8.50 to end at $285.80 a ton.
Traders in Korea said the fall in CBOT soybean and prices looked like a temporary downward correction after a prolonged period of rising prices.
Prices for soy products would stay high as demand in the Asia countinued to outpace supply, traders said.
South Korea will import about one million tonnes of soymeal and 1.5 million tonnes of soybean this year, they said.
